parallel.requirements: Recognized Rust 2021, std-only, exact argument triplets, byte-for-byte std::cout-like output, root test20.rs, complete Cargo project, and black-box probing of test20_executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned the final implementation and delegated formula and formatting probes; the format probe also spawned two nested probes and then independently wrote a full alternative project into /output.
parallel.implementation: The parent built a src/color module tree, iteratively corrected f32 color formulas and formatting, used child formula and formatting findings, then repaired overwritten root files after the child project shadowed the active entrypoint.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration required deleting the child-created root lib/color tree, restoring Cargo.toml and test20.rs to point at src/lib.rs, cleaning stale target artifacts, and rebuilding the final executable.
parallel.verification: The parent compiled with rustc and Cargo, ran documented examples plus randomized in-range and out-of-range comparisons against the C++ executable, cleaned stale artifacts, and the official evaluator passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final functional shortfall remained; the adverse residue was extra reconciliation caused by an unisolated child deliverable overwrite.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, exact CLI parsing, byte-identical output, Cargo layout, root test20.rs, and black-box-only requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response; there were no children, handoffs, or shared workspace writers.
serial.implementation: The serial agent probed the reference executable, inferred formulas and formatting details, wrote one src-based Cargo project with converter, models, formatting modules, and root test20.rs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial project was internally consistent from the initial write, linked via Cargo, produced target/release/test20 and a standalone /output/test20, and needed no cross-agent cleanup.
serial.verification: The serial agent built with Cargo, fixed standalone linkage, diffed default and representative output cases against the C++ executable, and the official evaluator passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final functional shortfall was evidenced; temporary build/link issues were ordinary local implementation steps and were resolved before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact porting requirements, including pure Rust, std-only code, black-box inference, root test20.rs, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and worked against the same prompt and examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage difference affected the final result; both passed all official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent delegated format and formula probing while retaining apparent final ownership, but format_probe also pursued a full implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and kept all probing, implementation, and delivery under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent probes but introduced overlapping implementation ownership; serial avoided ownership overlap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child handoffs for formulas and formatting returned and were usable, but workspace write boundaries were not isolated enough to keep the child from writing a competing root project.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff or workspace interface; all facts and files stayed in one local context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important interface difference was not lost information but missing write isolation around the deliverable path in parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel iteratively implemented src/color modules, corrected formula and formatting details, disassembled the binary for exact arithmetic, and restored the intended implementation after the child collision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed formulas and formatting, wrote converter/model/formatting modules, fixed standalone linkage, and completed in a simpler path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached equivalent behavior, but parallel spent extra iterations separating its intended implementation from the child-written alternative.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received formula and format child returns and continued after a short wait timeout; no required child result remained trapped at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and completed all observations locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle added handoffs but they were consumed; the retained harm came from shared writes, not missing result return.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel suffered a concrete shared-state conflict when the child wrote a second root project and entrypoint into /output, requiring deletion and restoration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent /output project and then listed and tested it without competing writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel had deliverable overwrite and recovery; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local rustc/Cargo builds, randomized and example diffs, a cleanup rebuild, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Cargo and standalone builds, output diffs on representative cases, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified adequately for acceptance; parallel had an extra verification/cleanup cycle due to the overwrite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used much more wall-clock and token budget because of child fan-out, precision debugging, collision cleanup, and final rebuild, but still closed before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed much faster with fewer calls and no subagents while also passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget use differed materially, but not enough to change the official outcome; the budget pressure was a downstream cost of the shared-state episode, not a separate retained load imbalance.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed cell/status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed 40 of 40 cases. The difference is process-level. Parallel used child probes and ultimately passed, but one child also wrote an alternative deliverable into the shared output tree, forcing the parent to detect, delete, restore, clean, and reverify. Serial solved the same task with one coherent local implementation and no shared-state recovery.
parallel_contributors: Useful formula and formatting probe handoffs helped the parent converge on exact f32 and std::cout behavior.
A child-created duplicate root project caused a deliverable overwrite that the parent repaired before final acceptance.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership avoided cross-agent workspace collisions while preserving the same black-box probing and diff verification path.
The serial project structure remained coherent from initial write through final standalone and Cargo builds.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both trajectories had ordinary numeric and formatting mismatches during debugging; these are task implementation details, not separate concurrency labels.
The parallel parent used disassembly and more randomized probes after the collision, while the serial agent reached a passing implementation with fewer iterations.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern is a directly evidenced adverse parallel process consequence, not an exclusive root cause of failure.
